records.source_finding: The perceiver P and perceptible property I follow 59.1, with a prima-facie evidential warrant. The defeater not_indicator(I) omits P and perceptual context.
records.cq_adjudication: The source undercutter asks about the circumstances in which the image is unreliable. A generic property name alone cannot distinguish one observer’s misleading circumstance from another observer’s reliable one.
records.example_adjudication: The book example and exception variant validate a single perceptual context, not independent observers of the same property.
records.remaining: Use a context-qualified I or separate graphs; for general multi-observer use, scope the unreliability defeater to observer/context and add independent-support controls like those now used for memory.

records.source_finding: The visible classification premise, defeasible category conclusion, and both critical questions match pp. 345–346. The root reviewer independently checked the original 2006 journal PDF pp. 324–325; this reviewer separately checked the supplied compendium.
records.cq_adjudication: misleading_appearance(O,C) undercuts misleading appearance in the proposed classification. more_justifiable_category(O,C) is a bounded existential/comparative defeater: evidence must show a better alternative category for this O/C claim, not merely some other category.
records.example_adjudication: The source fixture and exception variants cover both questions. No unbound alternative-category variable is introduced. Under this declared aggregate interpretation and the independent journal verification, the original-source hold can close.

records.cq_adjudication: All three printed undercutters are modeled as exceptions. CQ1–CQ2 now have P/M scope; CQ3 already had it. The source’s unusual wording of CQ2 is preserved rather than silently reinterpreted.
